title: CSS Flexbox Basics for Layout
description: Learn the essential CSS Flexbox properties for positioning and aligning elements on the screen. This tutorial covers the most commonly used layout patterns you'll encounter in interviews.

steps.title: Creating a Flex Container
steps.explanation:
Flexbox works with two concepts: the **flex container** (parent) and **flex items** (children).

To start using Flexbox, you set `display: flex` on the parent container. This automatically makes all direct children flex items that can be positioned with flex properties.

By default, flex items:
- Line up in a row (horizontal)
- Start at the left edge
- Stretch to fill the container's height

Think of the container as the 'director' that controls how its children are arranged. Once you set `display: flex`, you unlock powerful layout properties.
steps.task:
Create a component that:
1. Has a main `div` with inline style `{{ display: 'flex' }}`
2. Inside that div, create three child `div` elements with text 'Box 1', 'Box 2', and 'Box 3'
3. Give each child div an inline style with `{{ padding: '20px', background: '#e0e0e0', margin: '5px' }}` so you can see them

You should see three boxes lined up horizontally.
hints: Use inline styles in React: style={{ display: 'flex' }}
Create three separate div elements inside the flex container
Each child needs the padding/background/margin style to be visible

steps.title: Centering Items with justify-content
steps.explanation:
The `justify-content` property controls alignment along the **main axis** (horizontal by default).

Common values:
- `flex-start` - items at the start (default)
- `center` - items in the center
- `flex-end` - items at the end
- `space-between` - items spread out with space between them
- `space-around` - items with equal space around them

This is the property you'll use most for horizontal centering. Want to center something horizontally? Use `justify-content: center`.
steps.codeExample:
// Centering items horizontally
Centered!
steps.task:
Update your flex container to add `justifyContent: 'center'` to the inline style.

Your three boxes should now be centered horizontally on the screen.
hints: In React inline styles, use camelCase: justifyContent instead of justify-content
Add it to the same style object: {{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'center' }}
The boxes should move from the left edge to the center

steps.title: Vertical Centering with align-items
steps.explanation:
The `align-items` property controls alignment along the **cross axis** (vertical by default).

Common values:
- `stretch` - items stretch to fill container (default)
- `flex-start` - items at the top
- `center` - items vertically centered
- `flex-end` - items at the bottom

To perfectly center something both horizontally AND vertically, use:
```css
display: flex;
justify-content: center;  /* horizontal */
align-items: center;      /* vertical */
```

This is the most common interview pattern for centering!
steps.task:
Update your flex container to:
1. Add `alignItems: 'center'` to center items vertically
2. Add `height: '300px'` so there's vertical space to see the centering

Your boxes should now be centered both horizontally and vertically.
hints: Use camelCase: alignItems instead of align-items
You need both justifyContent and alignItems for full centering
The height gives vertical space to see the alignment

steps.title: Changing Direction with flex-direction
steps.explanation:
The `flex-direction` property changes the main axis direction.

Values:
- `row` - horizontal (default)
- `column` - vertical
- `row-reverse` - horizontal, reversed
- `column-reverse` - vertical, reversed

When you switch to `flex-direction: column`:
- Items stack vertically
- `justify-content` now controls VERTICAL alignment
- `align-items` now controls HORIZONTAL alignment

They swap! This confuses people at first, but remember: justify-content always works on the main axis.
steps.task:
Change your flex container to:
1. Use `flexDirection: 'column'` to stack items vertically
2. Keep the other properties (justifyContent, alignItems, height)

Now your boxes should be stacked vertically and centered.
hints: Use camelCase: flexDirection instead of flex-direction
With column direction, items stack top to bottom
The centering still works, but now justify-content centers vertically

steps.title: Spacing with gap
steps.explanation:
The `gap` property adds space between flex items automatically, without needing margins.

This is much cleaner than using margins on each child. You can use:
- `gap: '20px'` - same gap in all directions
- `gap: '20px 10px'` - different vertical and horizontal gaps (row-gap column-gap)

The `gap` property is modern and widely supported. It's the easiest way to add consistent spacing.

For interviews, knowing `gap` makes your CSS cleaner and shows you know modern CSS.
steps.task:
Update your flex container:
1. Remove the `margin: '5px'` from your child boxes (if you added it)
2. Add `gap: '20px'` to your flex container style instead

You should see consistent spacing between your boxes, controlled by the parent.
hints: Add gap to the flex container, not the children
Use gap: '20px' in the inline style object
Gap automatically adds space between items, not around them
